en: The *Lokeśvarastotra*: [I praise] the one of manifold forms, the virtuous refuge of the world,
who is necessarily embodied as Lokeśa, Keśava, Hara, and Ātman.
I worship the wise Śrī Lokanātha, the bestower of auspiciousness, whose eyes are as broad as lotuses and who enables one to cross the ocean of saṃsāra. ||1||
The protector of people afflicted by all fears, with a beautiful face and ears adorned with lovely golden earrings,
shining with necklaces and other jewel ornaments.
I worship the wise Śrī Lokanātha, the bestower of auspiciousness. || 2 ||

To the one who bestows boons, who is compassionate, the god above gods, the immortal, accompanied by the assembly of Jinas— who grants the cessation of calamities for the man who bows with devotion and bestows the fruits of heaven and liberation— [I pay homage].
I worship the wise Śrī Lokanātha, the bestower of auspiciousness. ||3||
To him whose forehead-mark is of the nature of intense heat, who is the ocean of jewels for the gods, whose hands are adorned with golden spears,
who is resplendent, and who bestows the directions by wearing ornaments—
I worship the wise Śrī Lokanātha, the bestower of auspiciousness. || 4 ||
To him who removes foul odors and miserable rebirths, who takes away misfortunes, who brings about the end of famine, the mine of compassion;
the bestower of knowledge, a treasury of virtues, whose body is auspicious and pure.
I worship the wise Śrī Lokanātha, the bestower of auspiciousness. || 5 ||
Thus [he praised] the excellent one, the sovereign of all hosts of beings, the lord of the three worlds, who is worshipped even by the immortals;
and so [he saw him] having comfortably entered his excellent chariot in a certain place.
I worship the wise Śrī Lokanātha, the bestower of auspiciousness. || 6 ||
Bowed down by all Yakṣas, Kinnaras, humans, sages, Nāgas, Vidyādharas, hosts of gods, Danujas, and Piśācas,
with their hands joined in reverence.
I worship the wise Śrī Lokanātha, the bestower of auspiciousness. || 7 ||
His limbs were beautifully adorned by being anointed with perfumes such as sandalwood, musk, excellent camphor, saffron,
and yellow sandalwood.
I worship the wise Śrī Lokanātha, the bestower of auspiciousness. || 8 ||
I worship him whose auspicious name destroys diseases and the like for those who take refuge in it,
who removes sorrows and other sufferings, who is to be contemplated with joy,
whose speech is like nectar, and whose body is naturally tender.
I worship the wise Śrī Lokanātha, the bestower of auspiciousness. || 9 ||
With hands reaching down to his knees, possessing the stature of a lordly elephant, the pinnacle of the pool of beauty, with teeth as bright as crystal,
he has an exceedingly beautiful body and limbs endowed with auspicious marks.
I worship the wise Śrī Lokanātha, the bestower of auspiciousness. || 10 ||

Those people who, being sincere in nature, shall always recite this fragrant hymn to the Lord of the World—Śrī Lokanātha himself, grasping it with his own hand, will swiftly grant their desired object. (11)
The *Śrīlokeśvarastotra* is complete.
